RECALL.basis: memory sentence names information the user lacks (M02-M04, M06-M10, M12)

EXPRESS.basis: memory cannot be turned into keyword/name/wording/description/narrowing (M02,M05,M06,M11,M12) or user contrasts with precise identifiers (C04)

MATCH.basis: date search returned too many results (B03) or many plausible results (C08); product output is otherwise rarely described

RECOGNIZE.basis: one-by-one opening, timeline/thumbnail scan, date-range comparison, similar-not-exact, cannot tell which is right (B04,B11,B13,B14,B16,C08)

RECOVER.basis: reformulation, switching, browsing fallback, several attempts, other app, gave up, failed (B05,B07-B10,B12,B15,B17,B18)

judgement_objects: a photo of my grandfather at the wedding
a photo of my grandparents' wedding album
a screenshot of a product I wanted
the lamp I wanted to buy
the photo from when I was sick
the picture I sent to my doctor

D1.name: Recall
D1.brief_question: What information do people actually remember, and what have they forgotten?
D1.user_behavior: Holds partial context (people, place, story, look, roughly when) but lacks a precise identifier
D1.product_outcome: n/a: this is the precondition the case starts from (photo exists, memory is incomplete)
D1.proposed_measure: Share of retrieval attempts that start with contextual clues but no precise identifier (date, name, album, exact keyword)

D2.name: Express
D2.brief_question: Is the user unable to express what they remember?
D2.user_behavior: Turns memory into a query, filter or navigation step
D2.product_outcome: The input the product receives carries the clues the user actually holds
D2.opportunity: O1 Memory expression (with O2 Approximate-time narrowing and O8 Information discovery)
D2.proposed_measure: Clues the user can state when prompted versus clues present in the first query (research); first-query length and clue types (production)

D3.name: Understand & match
D3.brief_question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues they provide?
D3.user_behavior: Submits clues and inspects what comes back
D3.product_outcome: The intended photo appears among the candidates returned
D3.proposed_measure: Target-in-candidate-set rate for tasks with a known target (research); selected photo appearing on the first results page (production)

D4.name: Evaluate
D4.brief_question: Are potentially relevant results difficult to evaluate?
D4.user_behavior: Scans candidates and decides which one is the photo
D4.product_outcome: The user confirms the right photo, quickly and with confidence
D4.proposed_measure: Candidates inspected before confirmation, time to confirm, wrong-photo confirmations, stated confidence (research); open-and-return counts (production)

D5.name: Refine
D5.brief_question: Does the user struggle to refine an unsuccessful search?
D5.user_behavior: Reformulates, switches strategy, browses, asks someone, or stops
D5.product_outcome: A failed first attempt still ends in success, or in an informed stop
D5.proposed_measure: Success rate after reformulation, queries before success, abandonment after N unsuccessful queries (production); what prompted each change (research)

D6.name: Available
D6.brief_question: Is the photo in the searchable library at all?
D6.user_behavior: Asks another person, switches app or device, or gives up
D6.product_outcome: Retrieval is possible: the photo exists in the library the user is searching
D6.proposed_measure: Share of unsuccessful retrievals where the photo is absent from the library (needs a library audit in research)

EXPRESS.question: How does the user convert that memory into a search or action?

MATCH.question: Does the product appear to surface plausible candidates?

RECOGNIZE.question: Can the user identify the intended photo among candidates?

RECOVER.question: What does the user do after the first attempt does not work?
